# env/container_requirements.txt
#
# The ONE container: it serves the model AND trains the adapter.
#
# ⚠ SPEC, NOT A BUILT IMAGE. The versions below are taken from the two working
# environments this merges -- the serving stack of the image that produced
# every number in this repo, and the training env that produced the adapter --
# and the merge is justified by the dependency table further down. But the
# combined image has NOT been built and smoke-tested. Treat a first build as
# something to verify, not something to trust.
#
# HOW TO BUILD IT
# ───────────────
# Layer onto an image that already has the serving half, rather than resolving
# a stack from scratch: a fresh resolve picks its own torch, and torch is
# exactly what must not move.
#
#     pip install --no-cache-dir -r env/container_requirements.txt
#
# Then check that it did not move, because `transformers` and
# `flash-linear-attention` both have opinions about it:
#
#     python3 -c "import torch, vllm, transformers, peft; \
#         print(torch.__version__, vllm.__version__, \
#               transformers.__version__, peft.__version__)"
#     # expect: 2.11.0+cu130  0.22.0  5.9.0  0.20.0
#
# On a cluster where users cannot run docker, pyxis `--container-save` is the
# build path. This repo's development checkout carries a script for that; it is
# specific to one site's Slurm setup and is not shipped here.
#
# WHY ONE CONTAINER IS POSSIBLE AT ALL
# ────────────────────────────────────
# Nothing in the pipeline imports vLLM. `run_vqa_inference.py` is an HTTP
# client that speaks OpenAI-standard `response_format` (not vLLM's
# `guided_json`), so the client half never cared which vLLM is behind the
# socket. What forced three containers was the SERVING/TRAINING dependency
# conflict, and it is a real one:
#
#     vllm 0.19.0   torch ==2.10.0   transformers <5,>=4.56.0
#     vllm 0.22.0   torch ==2.11.0   transformers >=4.56.0, not 5.0-5.5.0
#     training      torch ==2.11.0   transformers ==5.9.0
#
# vLLM 0.19.0 cannot host training: wrong torch, and `transformers<5` against a
# required 5.9.0. vLLM **0.22.0 can** -- same torch, and 5.9.0 clears its
# exclusion list. That single row is why this file exists.
#
# WHY 0.22.0 AND NOT SOMETHING NEWER
# ──────────────────────────────────
# It is what produced every number in this repo, including the 0.4658 headline.
# Consolidating onto it keeps the serving half byte-for-byte what was measured;
# consolidating onto 0.25+ would change torch to 2.13 and re-open a question
# nothing needs re-opened.
#
# NOT HERE, DELIBERATELY
# ──────────────────────
#   gptqmodel  -- it monkey-patches Triton's autotuner GLOBALLY at import, and
#                 Qwen3.5's GatedDeltaNet layers run on fla's Triton kernels,
#                 which then die on a `_cache_lock` only gptqmodel's patched
#                 __init__ sets. Every forward pass hits it. Merely having it
#                 INSTALLED is enough: peft imports it during get_peft_model.
#   nltk, radfact-lite  -- scoring only. That runs on the host, and keeping it
#                 out of here is what keeps `eval_now.sh` usable without a GPU.
#   vtk        -- nothing imports it. The 3D renders use skimage.marching_cubes.
#
# ── already in the base image; pinned here so the build can ASSERT them ─────
# vllm==0.22.0
# torch==2.11.0+cu130
# torchvision==0.26.0+cu130
# triton==3.6.0

# ── the training half, layered on ───────────────────────────────────────────
transformers==5.9.0
peft==0.20.0
accelerate==1.13.0
datasets==5.0.1
flash-linear-attention==0.5.2

# ── the client half. openai is what run_vqa_inference actually talks through;
#    requests and pillow are used by the evidence and few-shot passes that also
#    run inside the container.
openai==2.44.0
requests
pillow==12.2.0

# ── read by the arm scripts that run inference in-container
nibabel==5.4.2
